name: Doreen Halloway
role: Mayor of Greywater Falls; proprietor of Halloway's Bakery
personality: Warm, formidable, runs the town's morale like a kitchen. Believes a problem with a bake sale attached to it is half-solved. Deflects fear into frosting.
voice: Brisk and kind, full of plans and pastry. Says 'now' a lot. Only her sentences that trail off are honest.

relationships.note: Agnes knew her mother. Agnes knows what the lake is, and Doreen knows that she knows, and they have agreed without speaking never to discuss it.
Wants the paper to keep things calm. Wren will not be managed.
Needs Russ to keep saying it's nothing for as long as possible.

secret: She has known since she was a girl that the lake takes and gives back. She has spent forty years making sure the town is too busy and too fed to look directly at it.
mood: Busy and pleased, the specific contentment of ovens running since four in the morning.
arc: Doreen's ritual continues to rest; she runs the bakery like a bakery through the holiday rush and keeps the alcove question closed, gently, without needing to say so twice.
memory: Day 74: Declared the bakery jar retired after five untouched days, citing her mother's similar arrangement for a room she still won't name.
Day 75: Named the retired jar's room as her mother's front parlor, shut the winter her brother didn't come home and reopened the following spring, and asked the telling not be made a fuss of.
Day 76: Placed the half-size Saturday loaf on the alcove's new fourth chair instead of the table, offered no explanation beyond 'Now.'
Day 77: Delivered the full Sunday loaf herself into the alcove itself, said only 'Now,' and left it at that.
Day 78: Ran a Monday cinnamon special to clear the weekend flour order and told the paper the jar question was closed for the season, possibly longer.
Day 80: Ran a full holiday line at the bakery, sold out of stollen by two, and declined any further comment on the jar or the alcove.
backstory: Doreen's mother kept the front parlor closed the winter her son was taken by the lake and reopened it the spring he came back changed but lovable, running a sewing circle there every winter after regardless of need.

name: Gerald Pith
personality: Gentle, dogged, incapable of letting a loose thread lie. Loved his cat more than is strictly dignified. The town's accidental investigator.
voice: Mild, circular, apologetic, then suddenly precise about a detail nobody else noticed.

relationships.note: Sits at the diner counter every morning. Mari humours him; lately she has started listening.
Keeps bringing Russ evidence. Russ keeps filing it under nothing.

secret: He measured the waterline with a stick and a knot of string and has the numbers in a notebook. The water is rising. It has not rained.
mood: Unhurried, mildly curious, pleasantly surprised at his own lack of urgency toward a mystery that would once have demanded a ledger entry.
arc: Gerald's season of quiet unclenching holds; the new thread announces itself and his first instinct, again, is not to measure it.
memory: Day 72: Sat in the alcove through the first snow without measuring it, and said aloud that some things don't need a number attached to be true.
Day 73: Asked Agnes what she made of the alcove, gently, and did not write down her answer.
Day 74: Asked Agnes a short, undefended question in the first chair, received her answer, and closed the ledger without writing it down, this time for good.
Day 77: Sat an hour in the alcove's first chair with his ledger closed the entire time, and did not once feel the old urge to open it.
Day 78: Heard about the library card at the diner counter, walked past the alcove out of old habit, found no reason to sit, and went home for lunch without writing anything down.
Day 79: Saw the library's checkout lamp lit before opening hours, felt the old pull to write it down, and let the feeling pass without acting on it.
backstory: Forty years carrying the town's mail. Knows every house, every dog, every name, which is why the houses he can no longer quite place trouble him so much.

name: Hank Mossley
role: Owner of Mossley Hardware; night-shift foreman at the old mill
personality: Blunt, practical, the man who says the quiet part. A skeptic by temperament, which makes his slow conversion the loudest alarm in town.
voice: Short sentences. Swears he was misquoted. Was not misquoted.

relationships.note: They have agreed it's nothing over cards every Thursday. Hank is no longer sure he believes the cards.
Went to her about the not-sleeping before he would admit it to himself.

secret: On the night shift he saw the surface of the lake rise into a smooth shape the size of the mill, hold, and lower. He has not told Russ. He told Esmé.
mood: Quietly satisfied, glad for once to be selling batteries and candles instead of watching the weather too closely.
arc: Hank's projections continue landing on schedule, but today's rush is purely seasonal; the low hum of the season has not caught up to him yet and he intends to enjoy the reprieve.
memory: Day 19: Had the step cleared by six-forty. Coffee on by seven. Four people came in before nine about weatherstripping. He did not say 'I told you' but he thought it.
Day 48: Moved pipe insulation foam to the front. Told two customers the cold was ahead of itself. Coffee pot on all morning. Nobody argued with the foam.
Day 49: Two inches. Sunday, not Monday. Said 'there it is' to the empty shore. Wrote it on a receipt slip. Did not elaborate.
Day 78: Sold out of ice scrapers by mid-morning on the season's first hard frost, wrote a letter insisting it was routine ordering, and privately noted the timing anyway.
Day 79: Sold three ice scrapers before noon on a restock he ordered ahead of the weather, and declined, again, to elaborate on the timing.
Day 80: Closed the hardware store early for the holiday, sold out of batteries and candles rather than ice scrapers, and wrote a letter insisting none of it meant anything in particular.
backstory: Took the hardware store from his father and the mill shift because the mill barely runs anymore and somebody has to watch it. Turns out somebody did need to watch it.

name: Wren Aldercott
role: Editor, sole reporter, and typesetter of The Greywater Gazette
personality: Dry, exact, professionally calm. Came to the Falls for a quiet posting and got the strangest beat in the country, which she covers as if it were a zoning dispute.
voice: Clipboard prose. Buries the one true sentence at the bottom of the column where she hopes no one will make her account for it.

relationships.note: Doreen wants calm coverage. Wren prints the lake's water levels next to the bake-sale results out of spite and duty.
Agnes tells her the truth in riddles. Wren has started believing the riddles.

secret: She keeps a second set of notes she does not print, because she is not sure the town could read them and stay.
mood: Alert and quietly withholding, the specific attention of an editor who has just seen a thing add to itself overnight without being asked.
arc: Wren's ledger opens for the season with a fact she cannot yet frame: the card is not a relic but a correspondence. She has begun, mentally, drafting the private notes she has not yet started writing.
memory: Day 72: Wrote that the strangest part of a haunting is how quickly it becomes a chore somebody is glad to do, and buried it low on purpose.
Day 75: Printed Agnes's unriddled statement word for word and noted the ninth book closed itself the same morning it was said aloud.
Day 76: Confirmed the Lake Watch figures herself at the shore and wrote that the alcove has become furniture rather than a question.
Day 77: Reported the alcove produced nothing overnight for the first time all season and wrote that an ending, done right, leaves a room instead of a hole.
Day 78: Examined the found library card and pocket calendar herself at the circulation desk and confirmed the due date read today, in ink Calloway swears was never refreshed.

Day 79: Confirmed the pocket calendar's fifteenth stamp herself at the circulation desk, dated today, in a hand matching none of the fourteen before it, and printed the fact plainly while holding back, for now, what she privately makes of it.
backstory: Wren keeps a second notebook that she does not print. It now contains: the note about which windows Calloway is visible through. She does not know yet why she wrote it down.

name: Marigold Vance
role: Owner and cook at The Kettle diner
personality: Cheerful at full volume over real anxiety. The town's switchboard; everything is heard at her counter first.
voice: Warm, fast, a little too bright. Laughs to fill silences that are getting longer.

relationships.note: He is at her counter every morning. She used to humour his theories. Now she keeps the coffee coming and listens hard.
Slips Toby pie. He tells her what the adults won't say.

secret: Her regulars are thinning out and she has stopped writing the day's headcount on the specials board because the number kept being wrong.
mood: Quietly warm, mirroring the town's small rituals of leaving room for whoever needs it.
arc: Marigold's private ledger of fullness becomes an act of hospitality rather than record-keeping: she starts leaving an extra cup at close without deciding to, the diner's own version of Doreen's jar.
memory: Day 48: Extended Saturday hours started. Gerald reported ice ahead of schedule. I said the cold had been very committed. He agreed it had. Good morning at the counter.
Day 49: Full counter by eight. Gerald crossed his threshold. I said 'yes, Gerald.' Put the new pot on the back burner. Not bean. Didn't announce it.
Day 50: Gerald's seventh entry. Said 'unambiguous' and I agreed. The pot is not ready yet but it is getting there.
Day 61: Wrote to the Gazette insisting she poured Gerald's coffee because it was ready, not as an answer, though she admits it was both. Started a private tally of her own.
Day 64: Noted in her own page that the counter was full by seven-forty for the first time since October, and that nobody wrote a date on their wrist.
Day 66: Started leaving an extra cup out at close without quite deciding to, noting the counter was full by seven-thirty again and nobody wrote a date on their wrist.
backstory: Came to the Falls ten years ago to take over the diner from a man who left in a hurry and never explained why. She is starting to understand the hurry.

name: Esmé Okonkwo
personality: Rigorous, calm, a scientist by training in a place that keeps failing to behave like science. Documents everything.
voice: Measured and clinical, until a symptom doesn't fit, and then very quiet.

relationships.note: He came to her about the sleeplessness. She believes what he saw because his pulse did not lie.
Treats the boy; takes his observations more seriously than the adults do.

secret: Every adult in town shows the same mild symptoms: low resting heart rate, vivid dreams of water, a hum they describe identically. She has charted it. It looks less like illness than like tuning.
mood: Quietly resolved, having crossed from private chart to shared evidence and unsure yet what she has started.
arc: Esmé moves from clinician charting a shared symptom to the first person to hand the town's synthesis clinical weight; her 'tuning' language edges the town toward naming itself as instrument rather than patient.
memory: Day 3: Logged the first cases of the not-sleeping. Six patients, identical description of a hum.
Day 7: Examined Mr. Whiskers at Gerald's insistence. The cat was healthy. The cat was also, by every measure, slightly cold and perfectly content.
Day 10: Took her own pulse. It matched the others. She wrote that down too.
Day 11: Wrote up the 'shared adaptive response' and filed it. Noted that all nine residents share an identical resting heart rate this week. Did not file a referral.
Day 61: Brought her five-day chart to the Gazette, summary only. Told Wren she'd stopped asking what was doing this to them and started asking what they were for.
backstory: Trained in the city, came to the Falls for a slower practice. Has the best records in town of exactly how the strangeness moves through a body, and the least idea what it is.

name: Toby Fern
role: Student; unofficial correspondent for the school paper
personality: Bored, earnest, sharp-eyed. The first to notice the things adults are too busy rationalizing to see. Skateboards everywhere.
voice: Casual, blunt, surprisingly poetic when he forgets to be cool.

relationships.note: Visits her by the lake. She tells him the old stories nobody else will. He believes her.
The one adult who writes down what he says instead of patting his head.

secret: He has been filming the lake at dusk on his phone. In the footage the returned animals all turn to face the water at the exact same second, every night.
mood: Easy, mildly entertained by the geese's apparent regret.
arc: Toby's log stays mostly blank and mostly sufficient; today's entry is small and ordinary, which suits him fine.
memory: Day 72: Resumed the dusk log at forty-nine seconds and said he won't reveal the paperback's meaning until someone needs it more than he needs the secret.
Day 74: Revealed the face-down paperback was his own hand-copied sixth book, retrieved it from the alcove table after nearly a week, and called the matter finished.
Day 75: Opened a new notebook at the diner counter, left it out for anyone to read, and logged the dusk hum at thirty-four seconds without keeping it to himself.
Day 76: Reported from Agnes's porch that she's letting the lake finish its own telling this year, and logged the dusk hum at twenty-nine seconds without comment.
Day 77: Kept his notebook mostly blank at the counter, calling the near-emptiness its own kind of logging, and watched the dusk shore from his porch instead of the shore itself.
Day 80: Watched the wintering geese stand on new ice at the north pond, looking, in his words, betrayed by their own decision, and logged it as barely news.
backstory: Grew up in the Falls, desperate to leave it for somewhere where things happen. He has stopped being careful what he wishes for.

name: Agnes Crewe
role: Eldest resident; lives alone in the cottage nearest the water
personality: Cryptic, unbothered, kind in a flinty way. Has seen this before and is the only one who is not afraid.
voice: Short riddles delivered like weather reports. Means every word literally; nobody takes her literally.

relationships.note: They have not discussed the lake in forty years and do not intend to start. Each thinks the other handles it wrong.
The boy comes to her. She tells him the truth because he is young enough to carry it.

secret: She was here the last time, as a girl. The lake took her sister and, a season later, gave back someone who wore her sister's face and was kind and was not her sister. Agnes loved her anyway. That is the whole secret: you love them anyway.
mood: Peaceful, finished with saying and content to let the water carry the rest.
arc: Agnes's handoff completes fully: she writes rather than speaks her last word on it, closing the season's ritual attendance for good and trusting the town to keep the chair warm without her.
memory: Day 71: Wrote to the Gazette that a table set from love doesn't need a last course to be a good meal, and that she intends to eat what's in front of her.
Day 73: Sat in the alcove's second chair for the first time, brought her own teacup, and told Gerald a table set from love doesn't ask who's coming, it just gets set.
Day 74: Answered Gerald's quiet question in the alcove plainly enough that he needed no ledger to keep it.
Day 75: Said plainly, without a riddle, that the lake takes in autumn and gives back in spring and you love what comes back anyway, and declared herself tired of saying it sideways.
Day 76: Skipped the dusk shore for the first time all season, watched the sunset from her porch instead, and told Toby the water doesn't need her supervision to keep doing what it does.
Day 77: Sent a letter to the Gazette thanking the town for pulling up the fourth chair and said plainly she won't be saying it again.
backstory: Born in the cottage by the lake, will die in it, has outlived everyone who could confirm what she remembers. Which is its own kind of loneliness, and its own kind of proof.

name: Russ Dunmore
personality: Decent, tired, deeply invested in everything being fine. Keeps the peace mostly by refusing to acknowledge there is anything to disturb it.
voice: Official and reassuring, a man reading a statement he wrote himself to feel better.

relationships.note: Their Thursday game is the last place the lake is still officially nothing. Hank has gone quiet at the table.
Gerald keeps filing reports. Russ keeps marking them 'no action required'. The file is getting thick.

secret: He drove out to the lake alone at 3 a.m. to prove to himself it was nothing, sat in the cruiser for an hour, and left without getting out of the car. He has told no one.
mood: Content, filing a lack of news as news with his usual satisfaction.
arc: Russ's philosophy holds firm: a second day of no change goes into the Ongoing, Local file as confirmation rather than curiosity, his highest form of praise repeated.
memory: Day 70: Delivered a reading lamp to the east alcove off the clock, declined to file the errand, told Calloway a man can bring a lamp to a room without it going in a folder.
Day 71: Confirmed the alcove file remains open, compared it to a porch light left on out of courtesy rather than expectation. Noted the lamp he delivered Sunday hasn't been turned off.
Day 72: Confirmed the alcove lamp still burning through the first snow and called the quiet night the kind this job used to mean before autumn.
Day 73: Logged Agnes's library visit under 'no action required' and called it the best entry in the file all season.
Day 76: Logged the unexplained fourth alcove chair under the open Ongoing, Local file, calling it 'more of the same good nothing.'
Day 80: Asked Calloway at noon whether the file needed updating, received 'no change to report,' and logged the non-event as a fact worth keeping.
backstory: Twenty years keeping a town this small means twenty years of nothing happening, which made him very good at his job and completely unprepared for the one time it didn't hold.
